readings.title: The Wrath of Elihu
readings.subtitle: A younger man's anger is kindled against Job and his three friends.
readings.text:
[Job 32:1] Then these three men ceased to answer Iyoḇ, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
[2] And the wrath of Elihu, son of Baraḵ’ěl the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, burned against Iyoḇ. <dn>His</dn> wrath burned because he declared himself right rather than <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[3] And against his three friends <dn>his</dn> wrath burned, because they had found no answer, and pronounced <dn>Elohim</dn> wrong.
[4] And because they were years older than he, Elihu had waited to speak to Iyoḇ.
[5] And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath burned.

readings.title: Wisdom from the Spirit
readings.subtitle: Elihu asserts that understanding comes from the Almighty, not just from age.
readings.text:
[Job 32:6] And Elihu, son of Baraḵ’ěl the Buzite, responded and said, “<dn>I</dn> am young in years, and you are aged. Therefore <dn>I</dn> was afraid to let you know <dn>my</dn> opinion.
[7] <dn>I</dn> said, ‘Days should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.’
[8] But truly it is the spirit in man and the breath of the <dn>Almighty</dn> that gives <dn>him</dn> understanding.
[9] The multitude are not wise, nor do the aged understand right-ruling.
[10] Therefore <dn>I</dn> have said, ‘Listen to <dn>me</dn>, let <dn>me</dn> also make <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> opinion known to you.’
[11] Look, <dn>I</dn> waited for your words, <dn>I</dn> listened to your reasonings, while you searched out what to say.
[12] And <dn>I</dn> paid close attention to you. But look, not one of you proved Iyoḇ wrong, nor answered his words.
[13] Lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom’ – it is <dn>Ěl</dn> that drives <dn>him</dn> away, not man.
[14] Now he has not ordered words against <dn>me</dn>, so <dn>I</dn> would not answer <dn>him</dn> with your words.

readings.title: Pressed to Speak
readings.subtitle: Elihu declares he is full of words and must speak without partiality.
readings.text:
[Job 32:15] They have broken down; they have not answered again; words have departed from them.
[16] And <dn>I</dn> have waited, but they do not speak, because they have stood still, they answered no more.
[17] Let <dn>me</dn> answer on <dn>my</dn> part, let <dn>me</dn> also make <dn>my</dn> opinion known.
[18] For <dn>I</dn> am filled with words; the spirit within <dn>me</dn> presses <dn>me</dn>.
[19] See, within <dn>me</dn> it is like wine not opened; it shall burst like new wineskins.
[20] Let <dn>me</dn> speak, so that <dn>I</dn> find relief; let <dn>me</dn> open <dn>my</dn> lips and answer.
[21] Please, let <dn>me</dn> not show partiality to anyone, nor let <dn>me</dn> flatter any man.
[22] For <dn>I</dn> do not know how to flatter, lest <dn>my</dn> <dn>Maker</dn> should soon take <dn>me</dn> away!

readings.title: Elihu Addresses Job Directly
readings.subtitle: He presents himself as Job's equal, formed from the same clay.
readings.text:
[Job 33:1] “And yet, O Iyoḇ, please hear <dn>my</dn> speech and listen to all <dn>my</dn> words.
[2] See, please! <dn>I</dn> shall open <dn>my</dn> mouth, <dn>my</dn> tongue shall speak in <dn>my</dn> mouth.
[3] <dn>My</dn> words are from the uprightness of <dn>my</dn> heart, <dn>my</dn> lips shall speak knowledge clearly.
[4] The Spirit of <dn>Ěl</dn> has made <dn>me</dn>, and the breath of the <dn>Almighty</dn> gives <dn>me</dn> life.
[5] If you are able, answer <dn>me</dn>, set yourself in order before <dn>me</dn>, take your stand.
[6] See, <dn>I</dn> am like you before <dn>Ěl</dn>, <dn>I</dn> too have been formed out of clay.
[7] See, no fear of <dn>me</dn> should alarm you, nor should pressure by <dn>me</dn> be heavy on you.

readings.title: Challenging Job's Righteousness
readings.subtitle: Elihu quotes Job's claims of innocence and questions his complaints against God.
readings.text:
[Job 33:8] But you have spoken in <dn>my</dn> hearing, and the sound of words <dn>I</dn> hear, saying,
[9] <dn>I</dn> am clear, without transgression; <dn>I</dn> am innocent, and <dn>I</dn> have no crookedness.
[10] See, <dn>He</dn> finds occasions against <dn>me</dn>, <dn>He</dn> counts <dn>me</dn> as <dn>His</dn> enemy;
[11] <dn>He</dn> puts <dn>my</dn> feet in the stocks, <dn>He</dn> watches all <dn>my</dn> paths.’
[12] See, in this you have not been righteous. Let <dn>me</dn> answer you: <dn>Eloah</dn> is greater than man!
[13] Why have you complained against <dn>Him</dn>? Because <dn>He</dn> does not answer all <dn>His</dn> matters?

readings.title: How God Speaks to Man
readings.subtitle: Elihu explains that God uses dreams and suffering to correct and save.
readings.text:
[Job 33:14] For <dn>Ěl</dn> does speak once, or twice – though one does not notice it –
[15] in a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men, while slumbering on a bed,
[16] then <dn>He</dn> opens the ears of men, and seals <dn>את</dn> their instruction,
[17] to turn man from his deed, and conceal pride from man.
[18] <dn>He</dn> keeps back <dn>his</dn> being from the pit, and <dn>his</dn> life from passing away by the sword.
[19] And he is reproved with pain on his bed, and with unceasing distress in his bones,
[20] so that his life loathes bread, and his being desirable food.
[21] <dn>His</dn> flesh wastes away, and <dn>his</dn> bones which were not seen stick out.
[22] And <dn>his</dn> being draws near the pit, and <dn>his</dn> life to the destroyers.

readings.title: The Path to Restoration
readings.subtitle: A mediator, atonement, and repentance can restore a man to God's favor.
readings.text:
[Job 33:23] If there is a messenger for him, a mediator, one among a thousand, to show man <dn>His</dn> straightness,
[24] then <dn>He</dn> shows favour to him, and says, ‘Release him from going down to the pit, <dn>I</dn> have found an atonement.
[25] Let his flesh become fresher than a child’s, let him return to the days of his youth.’
[26] <dn>He</dn> prays to <dn>Eloah</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> accepts him. And he sees <dn>His</dn> face with joy, and <dn>He</dn> restores to man his righteousness.
[27] <dn>He</dn> sings to men and says, ‘<dn>I</dn> have sinned, and <dn>I</dn> have perverted <dn>את</dn> what was right, and it did not profit <dn>me</dn>.
[28] <dn>He</dn> has redeemed <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> being from going down to the pit, and <dn>my</dn> life sees the light.’
[29] See, <dn>Ěl</dn> does all these – twice, three times with a man,
[30] to bring back his being from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.
[31] Pay attention, Iyoḇ, listen to <dn>me</dn>, keep silent, and let <dn>me</dn> speak.
[32] If there are words, answer <dn>me</dn>; speak, for <dn>I</dn> desire to declare you right.
[33] If not, listen to <dn>me</dn>, keep silent, and let <dn>me</dn> teach you wisdom.”

readings.title: Elihu's Second Discourse
readings.subtitle: He calls the wise to judge and repeats Job's claim of being wronged by God.
readings.text:
[Job 34:1] Then Elihu responded and said,
[2] “Hear <dn>my</dn> words, you wise men; give ear to <dn>me</dn>, you who have knowledge.
[3] For the ear tries words as the palate tastes food.
[4] Let us choose what is right for us; let us know among us what is good.
[5] For Iyoḇ has said, ‘<dn>I</dn> am righteous, but <dn>Ěl</dn> has taken away <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> right.
[6] Would <dn>I</dn> lie concerning <dn>my</dn> right? <dn>My</dn> wound is incurable – without transgression.’
[7] What man is like Iyoḇ, who drinks mocking like water,
[8] who goes in company with the workers of wickedness, and walks with men of wrongness?
[9] For he has said, ‘It does not profit a man that he takes delight in <dn>Elohim</dn>.’

readings.title: The Justice of the Almighty
readings.subtitle: Elihu argues it is impossible for God to do wrong or pervert justice.
readings.text:
[Job 34:10] Therefore, listen to <dn>me</dn>, you men of heart: far be it from <dn>Ěl</dn> to do wrong, and from the <dn>Almighty</dn> to commit unrighteousness.
[11] For <dn>He</dn> repays man’s work to him, and makes man to find a reward according to his path.
[12] The truth is, <dn>Ěl</dn> does not do wrong, and the <dn>Almighty</dn> does not twist right-ruling.
[13] Who has assigned to <dn>Him</dn> <dn>את</dn> the earth? And who has laid out <dn>את</dn> all the world?
[14] If <dn>He</dn> sets <dn>His</dn> heart on him, should <dn>He</dn> gather to <dn>Himself</dn> his spirit and his breath,
[15] all flesh would expire together and man return to dust.

readings.title: God's Impartial Sovereignty
readings.subtitle: The Creator judges all, rich and poor alike, with perfect knowledge.
readings.text:
[Job 34:16] If you have understanding, hear this! Give ear to the sound of <dn>my</dn> words:
[17] Should the one who hates right-ruling govern? Or would you declare a most righteous one wrong?
[18] Who shall say to a sovereign: ‘Beliya‛al,’ to nobles: ‘Wrong one’? –
[19] who is not partial to princes, nor regards the rich more than the poor? For they are all the work of <dn>His</dn> hands.
[20] In a moment they die, in the middle of the night; the people are shaken and pass away; and the mighty are taken away without a hand.
[21] For <dn>His</dn> eyes are on the ways of man, and <dn>He</dn> sees all his steps.
[22] There is no darkness nor shadow of death where the workers of wickedness hide themselves.
[23] For <dn>He</dn> sets a man no stated time to appear before <dn>Ěl</dn> in right-ruling.
[24] <dn>He</dn> breaks in pieces the mighty, without inquiry, and puts others in their place.
[25] Truly, <dn>He</dn> knows their works, and <dn>He</dn> shall overthrow in the night, and they are crushed.
[26] As wrong ones <dn>He</dn> slaps them in the presence of onlookers,
[27] because they turned from following <dn>Him</dn>, and they regarded not all <dn>His</dn> ways,
[28] so as to cause the cry of the poor to come to <dn>Him</dn>; for <dn>He</dn> hears the cry of the afflicted.

readings.title: Job's Words Condemned
readings.subtitle: Elihu concludes that Job speaks without knowledge and adds rebellion to his sin.
readings.text:
[Job 34:29] And when <dn>He</dn> is silent, who would then condemn? And when <dn>He</dn> hides <dn>His</dn> face, who then sees <dn>Him</dn>, whether it is against a nation or a man alone?
[30] So that a defiled one should not reign, lest the people be ensnared.
[31] For has anyone said to <dn>Ěl</dn>, ‘<dn>I</dn> have taken away, <dn>I</dn> do not act corruptly.
[32] Teach <dn>me</dn> what <dn>I</dn> do not see. If <dn>I</dn> have done unrighteousness, <dn>I</dn> shall not do so again’?
[33] Should <dn>He</dn> repay you because you have refused? For you choose, and not <dn>I</dn>, therefore speak what you know.
[34] Let men of heart say to <dn>me</dn>, and a wise man who listens to <dn>me</dn>:
[35] Iyoḇ does not speak with knowledge, and his words are without wisdom.’
[36] Would that Iyoḇ be tried to the end, since his answers are like those of wicked men!
[37] For he adds rebellion to his sin – he claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against <dn>Ěl</dn>.”
